newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians protest for Israel to free prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians protest for Israel to free prisoners.

text.p: Hundreds of Palestinians demonstrated across the West Bank on Saturday to demand the release of Palestinian prisoners jailed in Israel, witnesses said.

Protesters staged rallies and sit-ins in the self-ruled Palestinian cities of Ramallah, Bethlehem, Nablus and Jenin and in Israeli-occupied Hebron and East Jerusalem to demand freedom for the some 4,000 prisoners Israel promised to release under peace deals with the PLO.

"We call on Israel to release prisoners and to implement agreements signed with the PLO, including redeployment from Hebron," Hebron Mayor Mustafa al-Natshe told a 400-strong crowd in the volatile city at the centre of deadlocked talks between the Palestine Liberation Organisation and Israel.
"There will be no peace without the Hebron redeployment and the release of prisoners," he told the rally.

At the end of a rally in Bethlehem, protesters threw stones at Israeli soldiers guarding Rachel's Tomb, a Jewish shrine adjacent to the autonomous town, witnesses said. Israeli soldiers fired tear gas and PLO police intervened to disperse the demonstrators. There were no injuries.
Israel has freed more than 5,000 Arab prisoners under its interim peace accords that set up Palestinian self-rule in parts of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
But further prisoner releases were frozen by a wave of Islamic militant suicide bombings that killed 59 people in the Jewish state last February and March.
The bombings also delayed an Israeli troop redeployment from Hebron, where 400 Jews live and study in heavily fortified compounds amidst 100,000 Palestinians.

Israeli-PLO talks on implementation of the Hebron pullback are stalled over Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's demand the deal signed by the government he ousted in May be modified to bolster safeguards for Hebron's Jews.
Palestinians reject any renegotiation of the signed deal.
The two sides each accuse the other of delaying an agreement.
